Chief Executive’s Monthly Management Report – 31st March 2026
 
 
A Chara,  
I enclose the above report for your statutory consideration, this report has also been prepared under Section 136 
& 138 of the Local Government Act, 2001. The attached report is the Chief Executive’s Monthly Management 
Report for March 2026, detailing activities, updates, and progress across various departments of Louth County 
Council. Below is a summary of key achievements and actions under various directorates from the Chief 
Executive Report for March 2026: 
 
1. Financial Management and System Support 
• 
Total expenditure: €40,349,703 out of €203,652,265 budget (20%).  
• 
Total income: €62,434,929 out of €203,652,265 budget (31%).  
• 
Annual Financial Statement: final adjustments underway, due to be presented at the April Council meeting. 
• 
IT helpdesk: 696 calls logged (01–30 March), 91.67% completed; most requests were Security and 
Application Software. 
• 
Email security: 14% of inbound emails flagged as potentially harmful (phishing/spam). 
• 
Cyber security training: focus on more sophisticated phishing (incl. AI-generated emails) and 
reporting/verification practices. 
2. Economic Delivery 
• 
Festival Grants 2026: 94 applications assessed; 77 offers issued; €200,000 committed. 
• 
St Patrick’s Day: parades supported in Ardee, Drogheda, Dundalk; Dundalk featured on RTÉ. 
• 
International promotion: delegation to Toronto & New York meeting Tourism Ireland/IDA/Enterprise Ireland 
etc., promoting Louth and the Dublin–Belfast corridor. 
• 
Local Enterprise Office: Local Enterprise Week ran 2–6 March; Enterprise Awards held; 1,453 students from 
19 schools in Student Enterprise Awards. 
• 
Planning indicators (reported for Feb 2026): 72 applications received (63 valid); 29 further-info responses; 
23 pre-planning requests. 
• 
Built heritage grants: 15 BHIS projects (€269,655.23) and 2 HTB projects (€14,392.23). 
• 
Forward planning: non-statutory consultation 18 March–8 April 2026 on lands to meet housing growth 
requirements took place along with the implementation of the 2027 County Development Plan. 
3. Operations and Environmental Delivery 
• 
Full works Programme is in the report, key highlights below: 
• 
Continue to mend potholes in the cunty due to the recent storm Chanda. 
• 
Dundalk & North Louth flooding/drainage: gully cleaning and drain/jetting works at multiple locations 
(e.g., Quay Street, Ramparts, Mournevale, etc.). 
• 
Dundalk road repairs: pothole repairs at 60+ locations. 
• 
Dundalk footpaths/crossings: repairs and upgrades; new crossings at Stapelton Place and Ecco Road. 
• 
Drogheda Gully Cleaning in preparation of St Patricks Day Parade at West St, Shop St & Peters St. 
• 
The Dept. of Transport has advised the allocation of funding for the Community Involvement Scheme (CIS) 
2026 is €286,550. 
• 
Local Improvement Scheme 2026 The Dept. of Rural & Community Development has advised funding of 
€372,890 for 2026 
• 
A review of the Casual Trading waiting list was carried out for Summer 2026. 
• 
Continuing to work with local fishermen in Port Oriel, Clogherhead regarding the ongoing unauthorised 
moorings with legal proceedings underway. 
• 
Hare’s Corner Project, Tree Council of Ireland and Coillte, hosted a Tree Handout Day 5,400 native trees 
were distributed to over 190 groups and individuals across the county. 
4. HR, Corporate & Community Delivery  
• 
In March 2026 Customer Services dealt with 17,565 queries inclusive of 8,684 calls, 986 e-mails and 7,895 
counter queries. 10,785 (61%) of queries received were dealt with at first point of contact.

• 
Gaeltacht Scholarship Awards were presented to fifteen students at a special Seachtain na Gaeilge 
celebration held in County Hall 
• 
Age Friendly Ambassador’s Day took place on the 4th March 2026. 
• 
To date, LEADER projects in Louth has allocated €1,262,278.01, which is 34.4% of the total programme 
budget. 
• 
Contracts for Louth’s PEACEPLUS Digital Arts Programme were signed. 
• 
A celebration of International Women’s Day took place in Fairs St Drogheda. 
• 
Dundalk Sports Centre launched ‘HER NIGHT’, a Women in Sport initiative for women to be active 
 
5. Housing and Culture Delivery 
• 
The Housing directorate continues to manage this area and achieve the goals set out in the Northeast 
Homelessness Strategy 2024-2026, see full report for details. 
• 
Significant strides have been made in homeless housing with rent subsegments, temporary emergency 
accommodation all being provided. 
• 
Rent arrears are monitored on an ongoing basis and letters are issued to customers within two weeks of their 
falling into arrears, currently ret arrears at €3.9 million, Rent income to date, is € 4,060,602.  7% increase when 
compared to the equivalent period in 2025 and 15% increase on 2024.  
• 
Cataloguing of local authority records continues with pre-1963 planning application records, publications 
regarding local government, and licence registers under the Cinematograph Act 1909. 
• 
Ireland Reading Campaign was hosted and the Right to read programme continues with Seachtain na Gaeilge 
activities included storytelling for Scoil Aonghusa, Irish music and singing parade through Drogheda Library.  
• 
Public Art Commissions, call for the three Artist in Residence commissions closed on 5th March, nine artists 
have been shortlisted to progress.  
 
6. Major Capital Projects and Infrastructure Delivery 
• 
The Urban Regeneration Development Fund (URDF) has now been replaced by the TCRIF, which was launched 
on 5th March with the intention of elements of the Westgate vision for this funding. 
• 
St. Nicholas Quarter continues with the redevelopment of and Bucklands Regeneration. 
• 
URDF call three has been announced a repeat survey of the 129 properties listed under URDF Call 3 is 
scheduled to take place mid-year. 
• 
A briefing consultation on Part 8 proposals for a playground in The Glen and St Dominics Park are taking place. 
• 
A new round of CLÁR funding for 2026 has opened. 
• 
Works will be commencing in the coming weeks on Railway Park, Ardee and Dundalk Demesne. 
• 
Works Phase 2 has commenced by the main contractor in March along with the Adress Castle. 
• 
Public Participation Days on the Flood Defence accorded for Blackrock, in March and Dundalk planned for April. 
 
I would again like to conclude by expressing my sincere appreciation for the exceptional commitment, resilience, and 
professionalism demonstrated by the entire Louth County Council team. Across all directorates, as staff continued to 
deliver high-quality public services, maintain critical operations to the county.  
 
I encourage all members to read the full report, which reflects the breadth and impact of the services that Louth Couty 
Council delivery daily. 
  
Regards

ArcGIS Online – Public Planning Register Map Viewer 
 
The LCC GIS Team recently updated the online Planning Register Map Viewers. These can be accessed from 
the Online Planning Application and Maps section user Services> Planning on the Louth County Council website.  
 
 
 
The data in the application is updated regularly to include all planning applications. There were 5,337 views of 
the application between 01/03/2026 and 30/03/2026, an average of 184 views a day in March. 
 
 
Cyber Security Training  
 
March’s cyber security training highlighted the increasing sophistication of phishing attacks, including the use of 
AI to create convincing emails. Staff were reminded to watch for pressure tactics such as urgency, authority and 
emotional triggers, to verify suspicious messages through independent channels, and to report concerns 
promptly. Real‑world examples showed how a single phishing email can lead to major operational disruption and 
significant financial loss.

Meitheal 2026 
 
 
The Council was represented at the Meitheal 2026 
event, which took place on 24th March at the 
Gleneagle Arena (INEC) in Killarney.  As Fáilte 
Ireland’s flagship travel trade workshop, Meitheal 
brings together Irish tourism businesses and 
international 
buyers 
to 
strengthen 
industry 
relationships and promote Ireland’s tourism offering.  
The Council’s presence at the workshop and the 
associated networking events ensured active 
engagement with key stakeholders and contributed 
to ongoing promotional efforts for the county. 
 
Boyne Valley Flavours (BVF) 
As part of Local Enterprise Week, Boyne Valley 
Flavours delivered the Food Business Beginnings: 
Real Producer Journeys event at the Ardee Food 
Hub.  The event was a great success, with over 30 
attendees joining for an engaging and informative 
session.  It provided valuable insights for early-stage 
food businesses, with a strong focus on real 
experiences, practical advice, and peer learning. 
 
The Centre of Food Culture Ireland 
The Centre of Food Culture Ireland hosted a 
delegation from the University of Gastronomic 
Sciences, Italy for a return study trip to the region 
from 7th to 12th March, for visits to 21 producers and 
hospitality providers in the region.  Visits included a 
morning in Carlingford Oyster Company, a tasting of 
Fierce Mild in Mo Chara in Dundalk, a foraging talk 
and lunch at The Glyde Inn and a visit to King of Kefir 
to learn about innovation coming down the line. 
 
The Centre of Food Culture Ireland launched its 
2026 educational events programme consisting of 
farm walks and meet the maker events across the 
country from April – October 2026, making a 
significant milestone in our development with events 
scheduled in Clare, Laois, Tipperary, Cork, Louth, 
and Meath. 
 
Boyne Valley Tourism

a speed networking event for their members at 
Monasterboice Inn.  This offered members an 
opportunity to network on a one-to-one basis and 
share information about their businesses with each 
other in a relaxed setting.  There was also talks from 
a digital marketing expert, Helen Leddy from Back 
Office Marketing Consultancy and Mary Dunne from 
Iregan Advisors about supports available to tourism 
businesses.
